proposal: The Mandate says enhanced statutory authority for local autonomy should extend to prioritizing rental subsidies that emphasize choice and mobility in vouchers over site-based subsidies, and to giving public housing agencies maximal flexibility to direct land sales involving existing public housing so land can be put to greater economic use. It asks Congress to consider the future of the public housing model, doubting that new investment beyond maintenance serves upward mobility, while cautioning that the turn to mobility vouchers must not come at the expense of local autonomy.
remaining: Statutory authority for broader PHA land sales for private use.

Notice PIH 2026-23, Demolition and/or Disposition of Public Housing Property
HUD updates guidance on demolition, disposition of public housing properties

status_summary: On 2026-07-11 Public Law 119-101 removed the 2029 expiration of the Rental Assistance Demonstration and raised its public housing conversion cap from 455,000 to 555,000 units (Section 212), moving more public housing to other rental assistance platforms; a CRS summary describes no provision on public housing land sales or voucher mobility. HUD Notice PIH 2026-23, issued 2026-08-28, eased demolition and disposition rules, including a very-small-PHA threshold raised to 75 units and functional obsolescence as a basis, while requiring fair market value for sales unless HUD approves a below-market transaction. The FY2027 budget request of 2026-04-03 would bar most new vouchers for new families, which runs against the mobility emphasis.

timeline.event: HUD's FY2027 budget request proposed barring most new vouchers for new families.
Public Law 119-101 removed the RAD expiration date and raised the conversion cap to 555,000 units.
HUD issued Notice PIH 2026-23, amending public housing demolition and disposition guidance.
